title: What is Code?
description: Why code? Why Claude? Why now? The philosophy behind lazy coding.

title: Your First Prompt
description: Claude basics. How to ask for code. The art of the prompt.

title: Set Up Your Workspace
description: VS Code, Node.js, terminal. The tools you need to ship code.

title: Variables & Types
description: Store data. Strings, numbers, booleans. Think like a filing cabinet.

title: Control Flow
description: If/else, loops, functions. Make your code think and repeat.

title: What Code Actually Is
description: What code really is (exact instructions, not magic), what happens when you run a program, why there are so many languages and why it barely matters yet, the gap between reading about code and writing it, and how to build a coding practice around a body with variable energy instead of against it.

title: A Setup That Works From Bed
description: Getting a real, working coding environment in place — starting with a browser-based editor that needs nothing installed, then an installed editor when you're ready, five terminal commands, where files actually live, and settings tuned for low light, low energy and one working hand.

title: Your First Programs
description: Writing, running and changing small programs that produce visible output — console.log, predicting a change before making it, comments written for next week's you, breaking things on purpose to learn their edges, and typing less on purpose.

title: Errors Are Information
description: Reading an error message as a precise, neutral diagnostic instead of a verdict — the difference between a syntax error and a runtime error, how far a program got before it failed, reading a stack trace to find your own code among the noise, and searching an error usefully once you understand what it's actually saying.

title: Asking an AI for Help, Well
description: Getting genuinely useful coding help from an AI tool: what to include so the answer is about your actual problem, asking for an explanation instead of just a fix, checking an answer you don't fully understand yet, recognizing confident-but-wrong answers, and learning from a solution instead of only pasting it.
